meta.name: Nashik District Soil Types
meta.disclaimer: Soil taxonomy simplified to six practical classes for decision support. Real farm decisions require soil testing; these classes are INITIAL ASSUMPTIONS pending validation against NBSS&LUP / Maharashtra land resource maps.

sources.label: Initial domain assumption (Phase 0) - pending NBSS&LUP soil map validation

soils.name: Deep Black Soil
soils.description: Deep clayey black cotton soil with high water retention and slow drainage.
notes: Can become waterlogged in high-rainfall years; difficult to work when wet.

soils.name: Medium Black Soil
soils.description: Moderately deep black soil, the workhorse of central Nashik agriculture.
notes: Widely used for onion, grapes, pomegranate under irrigation.

soils.name: Shallow Black Soil
soils.description: Thin black soil over weathered basalt, low moisture holding capacity.
notes: Best suited to hardy rainfed crops such as bajra.

soils.name: Alluvial Loam
soils.description: Fine loamy river-basin soil along Godavari and tributaries, naturally fertile.
notes: Premium horticulture belts (grapes, vegetables) cluster on these soils.

soils.name: Laterite / Reddish Hill Soil
soils.description: Reddish, iron-rich, well-drained soil of the western hilly belt.
notes: Terraced paddy and millets dominate; fertility depends heavily on organic matter.

soils.name: Sandy Loam
soils.description: Light-textured, fast-draining soil found in drier eastern tracts.
notes: Requires careful water management; suits hardy crops.
